findings.title: Cancellation and new scheduling race within same cron run
findings.body: The cron job first cancels reminders flagged `cancelled: true` scheduled within the next hour, then later finds unscheduled reminders and schedules new emails. There's no check that excludes already-cancelled bookingUids/workflowStepIds from this unscheduled-reminders query, so if a reminder was cancelled (cancelled=true) but not yet caught by the 1-hour window pass, it could still be picked up and sent since the `unscheduledReminders` query filters only on `scheduled: false` without excluding `cancelled: true` reminders. This re-introduces a path for cancelled reminders to be sent.

findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder swallows errors silently affecting data integrity
findings.body: The function wraps all branches in a single try/catch that only logs to console on failure. If the prisma update to set `cancelled: true` fails (e.g. transient DB issue), the reminder remains scheduled with no retry or alerting, meaning the workflow reminder could still fire for a cancelled/rescheduled booking undetected, since callers of this function don't check/await its result for error handling (it's called without awaiting in handleCancelBooking.ts and others).

findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/SMS calls not awaited
findings.body: The forEach loop calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting the promises. Since the cancel API handler returns right after, and these calls perform async DB writes (setting `cancelled: true`), the response may complete before the cancellation flag is actually persisted, increasing the race window where the cron job's query (within the same cron tick) might miss marking it cancelled before the response is used by the client to assume cancellation succeeded fully. It also means errors are not propagated to the caller for retries/logging context tied to the specific booking cancellation flow.

findings.title: Deleted reminders no longer deleted from DB in update handler
findings.body: Previously, after cancelling scheduled reminders when event types are removed from a workflow, the code also deleted the WorkflowReminder DB rows (`deleteReminderPromise`/`ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`). This deletion was removed; now only `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called, which for EMAIL just sets `cancelled: true` (not deleted) unless `immediateDelete` is passed (it is not passed here). This leaves orphaned/stale WorkflowReminder rows relying entirely on the cron job to clean them up and relies on the cron window logic working correctly; if an eventType is removed well before the one-hour cutoff, the reminder would remain unresolved for a long time and SMS reminders are deleted immediately via `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which does prisma.delete) causing inconsistent behavior between EMAIL and SMS method cleanups.

findings.title: SMS reminder deleted immediately while email reminder is only soft-cancelled
findings.body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder immediately deletes the WorkflowReminder DB row and cancels the Twilio SMS synchronously, whereas deleteScheduledEmailReminder (non-immediate) only sets `cancelled: true` and defers actual cancellation to the cron job. This asymmetry means the fix described in the PR (relying on cron-based batched cancellation to avoid hitting the SendGrid 100-pending-cancellation limit) does not apply to SMS cancellation at all, and the SMS path still directly calls the provider's cancel endpoint synchronously on every cancellation/reschedule, which could reintroduce the same kind of rate/pending-limit issue for Twilio if it exists, with no explanation on why this discrepancy exists or is safe.
